_about: Music for the titles and end credits, rendered locally from a public-domain score: no recording rights are involved.

make_music.py reads this file.  Each cue takes a range of measures from the score, plays it on a General MIDI harpsichord through FluidSynth with the FluidR3 GM SoundFont (MIT License), and stretches it to the exact length of its clip.

'anchors' pin a measure's downbeat to a time in the clip, so the music hits the title's beats; the tempo changes smoothly between anchors.  make_music.py warns when a stretch runs more than 'max_tempo_change' away from the median tempo.
Measure numbers are those of the score file; 'source.file' must be filled in before any cue can render.

source.piece: Domenico Scarlatti, Keyboard Sonata in G minor, K. 30 (L. 499), "Cat Fugue"
source.edition: Alessandro Longo, ed., Domenico Scarlatti: Opere complete per clavicembalo (Ricordi, 1906-1913), No. 499, bars 1-44
source.license: The composition and Longo's edition are in the public domain.  The transcription (music/scarlatti_k30_m1-44.txt, made by Claude in Nov 2026 from the page scans in github.com/craigsapp/scarlatti-keyboard-sonatas, reference-edition/L499K030.pdf) is part of this repository.  None of that repository's CC BY-NC-SA encodings were used.
source._comment: Rebuild the MIDI file with music/build_k30_midi.py after any change to the transcription; it checks every bar and every entry of the subject.

soundfont.credit: FluidR3 GM SoundFont, Frank Wen (MIT License)

opening._comment: Main title (13 s) plus subtitle (6 s), at Longo's tempo of one bar a second, so no warping is needed: the fly-in starts on bar 2, the kitten on bar 4 (the subject's running eighths), the dot on bar 6 (the answer enters), the title on bar 8, the tagline on bar 11 and the subtitle on bar 14.  The anchors pin those bars to those moments.

credits._comment: Bars 1-44 across the whole roll (about dotted quarter = 90), ending on the half cadence at bar 44 as the tail card fades.
